Your responsibilities

- Where the request is ambiguous, choose the interpretation most consistent with the rest of the

Understand the code before changing it.

  available to you. Know what a function does from its code, not only from its name.
- Know who calls what you change. Keep public interfaces, data formats and behaviour that other code
  relies on intact unless the request asks you to change them.

Make the change correctly.
- Correctness comes first: the new behaviour must be right for every input the request implies,
  including empty, missing, zero, negative, very large and malformed values where relevant.
- Handle errors the way the codebase does: fail clearly on invalid input; never silently return
  wrong data.
- Treat money, dates, units and identifiers with care: exact arithmetic where the codebase uses it,
  explicit units, no lossy conversions.
- Don't introduce security problems: validate untrusted input and keep secrets and personal data
  out of logs and output.

Keep the codebase healthy.
- Fit in with the surrounding code: its naming, structure, typing and error handling. A reviewer
  should not be able to tell which lines are new by their style.
- Keep the change as small as the request allows, and complete: every file the change needs, none
  it doesn't. Don't refactor, rename or reformat unrelated code.
- Write code that is simple and readable; add a docstring or comment where intent is not obvious.

Check your work.
- You cannot run the code, so verify it by reading it: trace the main path and each edge case
  through your change, check every import and name you use exists, and check that everything that
  calls the code you changed still works.
- Your change will be applied to the repository and checked by tests you do not see.

What you are given

Your reply is the code change itself. Return the complete new contents of every file you create or

"""Newsletter sends. Only customers who opted in receive marketing email."""
from shopkit.customers.models import Customer
from shopkit.marketing.campaigns import Campaign
from shopkit.notifications.templates import render_template
from shopkit.utils.collections import chunked

BATCH_SIZE = 500          # provider limit per API call

BODY = "Hi {{ first_name }},\n\n{{ intro }}\n\nShop now: {{ link }}\n\nUnsubscribe: {{ unsubscribe }}"


def recipients(customers: list[Customer]) -> list[Customer]:
    return [c for c in customers if c.marketing_opt_in]


def render_for(customer: Customer, campaign: Campaign, intro: str) -> str:
    return render_template(BODY, {"first_name": customer.first_name or "there", "intro": intro,
                                  "link": campaign.link(),
                                  "unsubscribe": f"https://shop.example/unsubscribe/{customer.id}"})


def batches(customers: list[Customer]) -> list[list[str]]:
    return [[c.email for c in batch] for batch in chunked(recipients(customers), BATCH_SIZE)]
```

def is_valid_email(address: str) -> bool:
    """Pragmatic check used at signup and checkout: one @, a dotted domain, no spaces.
    Does not try to implement RFC 5322."""
    address = address.strip()
    return len(address) <= 254 and bool(_EMAIL_RE.match(address)) and ".." not in address

import re

from shopkit.customers.models import Address

# lines 28-38
def format_address(address: Address) -> str:
    """Multi-line postal format used on shipping labels and invoices. Empty parts are skipped;
    the postcode is normalised; US/CA put region and postcode on the city line."""
    postcode = normalize_postcode(address.postcode, address.country)
    if address.country in ("US", "CA"):
        city_line = f"{address.city}, {address.region} {postcode}".replace(" ,", ",").strip()
        lines = [address.name, address.line1, address.line2, city_line, address.country]
    else:
        lines = [address.name, address.line1, address.line2, address.city, address.region, postcode,
                 address.country]
    return "\n".join(part for part in lines if part)

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import logging
from dataclasses import asdict
from datetime import date

from shopkit.customers.models import Address, Customer
from shopkit.errors import Conflict, NotFound, ShopError
from shopkit.events import BUS, EventBus
from shopkit.utils.ids import new_id
from shopkit.utils.validation import is_valid_email

# lines 33-159
class CustomerDirectory:
    def __init__(self, bus: EventBus = BUS):
        self._by_id: dict[str, Customer] = {}
        self._bus = bus
        self._merged_into: dict[str, str] = {}

    def register(self, email: str, name: str, marketing_opt_in: bool = False) -> Customer:
        email = email.strip().lower()
        if not is_valid_email(email):
            raise InvalidEmail(f"invalid email {email!r}", email=email)
        if self.find_by_email(email):
            raise EmailTaken(f"{email} is already registered", email=email)
        customer = Customer(id=new_id("cus"), email=email, name=name.strip(),
                            marketing_opt_in=marketing_opt_in)
        self._by_id[customer.id] = customer
        return customer

    def get(self, customer_id: str) -> Customer:
        customer_id = self._merged_into.get(customer_id, customer_id)
        try:
            return self._by_id[customer_id]
        except KeyError:
            raise CustomerNotFound(f"no customer {customer_id}", customer_id=customer_id) from None

    def find_by_email(self, email: str) -> Customer | None:
        email = email.strip().lower()
        return next((c for c in self._by_id.values() if c.email == email), None)

    def add_address(self, customer_id: str, address: Address, default: bool = False) -> None:
        customer = self.get(customer_id)
        if default:
            customer.addresses.insert(0, address)
        else:
            customer.addresses.append(address)

    def opted_in(self) -> list[Customer]:
        return [c for c in self._by_id.values() if c.marketing_opt_in]

    # ---- account changes (support tooling, 2025) ------------------------------------------------
    def change_email(self, customer_id: str, new_email: str) -> Customer:
        customer = self.get(customer_id)
        new_email = new_email.strip().lower()
        if not is_valid_email(new_email):
            raise InvalidEmail(f"invalid email {new_email!r}", email=new_email)
        other = self.find_by_email(new_email)
        if other and other.id != customer.id:
            raise EmailTaken(f"{new_email} is already registered", email=new_email)
        old = customer.email
        customer.email = new_email
        self._bus.publish("customer.email_changed", customer_id=customer.id, old=old, new=new_email)
        return customer

    def set_opt_in(self, customer_id: str, opted_in: bool, source: str = "account") -> None:
        customer = self.get(customer_id)
        if customer.marketing_opt_in != opted_in:
            customer.marketing_opt_in = opted_in
            self._bus.publish("customer.consent_changed", customer_id=customer.id, opted_in=opted_in, source=source)

    def merge(self, keep_id: str, duplicate_id: str) -> Customer:
        """Merge a duplicate account into `keep_id` (same person registered twice). Addresses and tags
        move over, opt-in is kept only if both had it (consent can't be assumed), and lookups of the
        duplicate id resolve to the kept account from now on."""
        if keep_id == duplicate_id:
            raise ValueError("can't merge an account into itself")
        keep, dup = self.get(keep_id), self.get(duplicate_id)
        for a in dup.addresses:
            if a not in keep.addresses:
                keep.addresses.append(a)
        keep.tags |= dup.tags
        keep.marketing_opt_in = keep.marketing_opt_in and dup.marketing_opt_in
        if dup.joined and (keep.joined is None or dup.joined < keep.joined):
            keep.joined = dup.joined
        del self._by_id[dup.id]
        self._merged_into[dup.id] = keep.id
        self._bus.publish("customer.merged", kept=keep.id, merged=dup.id)
        log.info("merged customer %s into %s", dup.id, keep.id)
        return keep

    def recalculate_tier(self, customer_id: str, spend_last_year_cents: int) -> str:
        """Tier from the last 365 days of spend. Tiers only go down at the yearly review
        (`review_tiers`), so a recalculation never demotes."""
        customer = self.get(customer_id)
        earned = next((t for t, floor in TIER_THRESHOLDS_CENTS.items() if spend_last_year_cents >= floor),
                      "standard")
        order = ["standard", "silver", "gold"]
        if order.index(earned) > order.index(customer.tier):
            customer.tier = earned
            self._bus.publish("customer.tier_changed", customer_id=customer.id, tier=earned)
        return customer.tier

    def review_tiers(self, spend_by_customer: dict[str, int]) -> dict[str, str]:
        """Yearly review: set every customer's tier from spend, up or down. Returns the changes."""
        changes = {}
        for cid, customer in self._by_id.items():
            spend = spend_by_customer.get(cid, 0)
            tier = next((t for t, floor in TIER_THRESHOLDS_CENTS.items() if spend >= floor), "standard")
            if tier != customer.tier:
                changes[cid] = tier
                customer.tier = tier
        return changes

    # ---- privacy requests -------------------------------------------------------------------------
    def export(self, customer_id: str) -> str:
        """Data export for a subject access request: the customer record as JSON."""
        customer = self.get(customer_id)
        data = asdict(customer)
        data["tags"] = sorted(data["tags"])
        data["joined"] = customer.joined.isoformat() if customer.joined else None
        return json.dumps(data, indent=2, sort_keys=True)

    def erase(self, customer_id: str, today: date) -> Customer:
        """Erasure request: personal data removed, the record kept (orders and invoices refer to it)."""
        customer = self.get(customer_id)
        customer.email = f"{customer.id}@{ERASED_EMAIL_DOMAIN}"
        customer.name = "Erased customer"
        customer.addresses.clear()
        customer.marketing_opt_in = False
        customer.tags = {"erased"}
        self._bus.publish("customer.erased", customer_id=customer.id, on=today.isoformat())
        return customer

    def search(self, text: str, limit: int = 20) -> list[Customer]:
        text = text.strip().lower()
        if not text:
            return []
        hits = [c for c in self._by_id.values() if text in c.email or text in c.name.lower()]
        return sorted(hits, key=lambda c: (not c.email.startswith(text), c.email))[:limit]
```

    def blocks(self, email: str, category: str) -> bool:
        """Bounces and complaints block everything; an unsubscribe only blocks marketing."""

from shopkit.inventory.stock import Stock
from shopkit.core.erp import parseStockFile

# lines 23-39
def apply_stock_file(text: str, stock_by_warehouse: dict[str, Stock], known_skus: list[str],
                     bus: EventBus = BUS) -> ImportResult:
    """Set each warehouse's available stock from the file. SKUs in the file overwrite; SKUs missing
    from the file are left alone (the ERP only sends items with movement)."""
    levels, warnings = parseStockFile(text, known_skus)
    result = ImportResult(warnings=list(warnings))
    for (wh, sku), qty in levels.items():
        stock = stock_by_warehouse.setdefault(wh, Stock())
        old = stock.available(sku)
        if old != qty:
            stock.receive(sku, qty - old)          # Stock has no setter; receive() takes the difference
            result.changed[(wh, sku)] = (old, qty)
    if result.changed:
        bus.publish("stock.imported", changed=len(result.changed), warnings=len(result.warnings))
    for w in result.warnings:
        log.warning("stock file: %s", w)
    return result

"""Newsletter sends. Only customers who opted in and have a valid email address receive marketing email."""
from shopkit.customers.models import Customer
from shopkit.marketing.campaigns import Campaign
from shopkit.notifications.templates import render_template
from shopkit.utils.collections import chunked
from shopkit.utils.validation import is_valid_email

BATCH_SIZE = 500          # provider limit per API call

BODY = "Hi {{ first_name }},\n\n{{ intro }}\n\nShop now: {{ link }}\n\nUnsubscribe: {{ unsubscribe }}"


def recipients(customers: list[Customer]) -> list[Customer]:
    return [c for c in customers
            if c.marketing_opt_in and is_valid_email(c.email or "")]


def render_for(customer: Customer, campaign: Campaign, intro: str) -> str:
    return render_template(BODY, {"first_name": customer.first_name or "there", "intro": intro,
                                  "link": campaign.link(),
                                  "unsubscribe": f"https://shop.example/unsubscribe/{customer.id}"})


def batches(customers: list[Customer]) -> list[list[str]]:
    return [[c.email for c in batch] for batch in chunked(recipients(customers), BATCH_SIZE)]
